parts.name: connect4_score
parts.original_hypothesis: The direct positional values and gated corrections add in the logit before the sigmoid produces predicted x-win probability. Their combined nonlinearity matters: replacing the switching gates by least-squares affine fits on the training rows changes AUC from 0.9189 to 0.8554. This does not identify which game tactics they represent. On the 765 training positions with an open three-o line pattern and a blank completion square, the observed x-win fraction is 26% while mean predicted x-win probability is 42%. The pattern definition does not require gravity support for the blank square. The dataset excludes forced-next-move positions; this subgroup is not a test of detecting an immediate winning move. In the constructed bottom-c-square edit, the whole-model predicted x-win probabilities for o, blank and x are 92%, 91%, 94%, respectively; this is an artificial coordinate edit, not a legal move sequence. The operation hierarchy is complete; maximum function-preservation error is 1.7e-15. The separate gate hypotheses remain descriptions rather than tactical explanations.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient); an input the data ties to a category takes its typical value within that category (linked inputs)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording

summary.text: The model treats a higher square c5 as clearly lowering the predicted chance that x wins in an uneven way: for a typical position, it goes from about 91% at empty to about 10% at x (the first player) (with square c1 (column c, row 1 from the bottom; x = +1, empty = 0, o = -1) at x (the first player) and square c2 (column c, row 2 from the bottom; x = +1, empty = 0, o = -1) at x (the first player) and square c3 (column c, row 3 from the bottom; x = +1, empty = 0, o = -1) at o (the second player) and square c4 (column c, row 4 from the bottom; x = +1, empty = 0, o = -1) at o (the second player), as in the data).

The model treats a higher square b6 as clearly lowering the predicted chance that x wins in an uneven way: for a typical position, it goes from about 91% at empty to about 14% at x (the first player), flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher.

The model treats a higher square a6 as clearly lowering the predicted chance that x wins in an uneven way: for a typical position, it goes from about 91% at empty to about 30% at x (the first player), flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher.

Through one part of the model, the square g6 adds to the predicted chance that x wins from empty (between -0.6 and 0.1 on the o-to-x scale for different positions) upwards (for 25630 of the 54045 training positions it already changes below that): for a typical such position, going from o (the second player) to empty moves it from about 8% to about 91% (on the training data only).

A higher square c5 clearly lowers the predicted chance that x wins, and even more so if square d1 is at or below empty (in an uneven way for patients with square d1 at or below empty): for a typical position, square c5 going from empty to x (the first player) moves the predicted chance that x wins from about 91% to about 10% if square d1 is at or below empty, and from about 95% to about 83% if square d1 is above empty.
